newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania engineer selloff share to trade on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Romania engineer selloff share to trade on bourse.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Tuesday mass selloff shares in listed Artrom SA state-run engineering firm could be traded starting on Thursday.
Individuals who got Artrom shares in exchange for coupons under the mass privatisation can start trading them on the bourse through securities companies, a bourse statement said.
Romania launched the mass selloff a year ago, allowing Romanians to swap privatisation paper for stakes of up to 60 percent of 4,000 state companies.
Bourse sources said 1,573 Romanians subscribed for Artrom, getting a total of more than 60,000 shares for their coupons.

Artrom, based in the southwestern town of Slatina, has a share capital of 141.33 billion lei. Before the start of subscription, the State Ownership Fund was its majority 70 percent shareholder, a private fund had 13.41 percent and employees and other stockholders held the rest.

Brokers and bourse officials see mass privatisation shares as gradually offering a partial solution to the liquidity squeezes which plagued the exchange in recent months, bringing turnover and prices down.

Artrom's half-year report showed its profit down to 196.6 million lei from 228.8 million in the same period of 1995, due to burdening interest on loans and financial bottlenecks in the economy, which delayed payments from its end-users. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
